appraisal_events.evidence: « Monsieur a une facilité de parole, une mémoire ! ... comme j'en ai rarement rencontré. ... Il ferait un excellent prédicateur. ... je n'ai pas souvent vu tenir le crachoir avec une pareille dextérité »
appraisal_events.explanation: Forcheville lavishly praises the painter's eloquence and memory to Mme Verdurin, going so far as to suggest he might even outdo the esteemed professor Bréchot.

appraisal_events.evidence: « le seul nom de personnes qu'ils ne connaissaient pas était accueilli chez eux par un silence réprobateur », following Forcheville's mention that Swann is always at the La Trémoïlle's and the Laumes'; Mme Verdurin concludes, « On me paierait bien cher que je ne laisserais pas entrer ça chez moi », en regardant Swann d'un air impérieux.
appraisal_events.explanation: Forcheville's attempt to flatter Swann by naming his grand aristocratic connections meets the clan's disapproving silence, and Mme Verdurin closes by declaring such people unwelcome in her house while fixing Swann with an imperious look, implicitly warning him that this outside prestige counts against him here.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Ce n'était plus qu'une cire perdue, qu'un masque de plâtre, qu'une maquette pour un monument, qu'un buste pour le Palais de l'Industrie », with « une majesté presque papale », until « le marbre finit par s'animer » to say the La Trémoïlle wife « était toujours ivre » and the husband said « collidor pour corridor ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator mocks Mme Verdurin's frozen performance of wounded dignity with an inflated, ironic statuary simile, and the irony sharpens the instant her supposed marble 'majesty' comes to life to deliver a crude, petty insult, exposing rather than confirming the superiority she is staging.

status_effects.explanation: Forcheville's extended, specific praise elevates the painter's local standing as a remarkably eloquent talker, worth comparing to Bréchot.

The clan's disapproving silence at hearing of Swann's grand-society connections, and Mme Verdurin's explicit declaration that such people are unwelcome, register a witnessed dip in how his outside prestige counts within this milieu.
Mme Verdurin's pointed, imperious look directed straight at Swann as she delivers her warning puts him in an implicitly subordinate, dependent position within the clan.
By delivering the warning and fixing Swann with an imperious stare, Mme Verdurin visibly asserts control over the terms of his continued welcome.
The narrator's ironic statue simile deflates Mme Verdurin's performed dignity, exposing wounded pride and petty snobbery-in-reverse rather than the majesty it superficially describes.

ambiguities: Forcheville's aside comparing 'le peintre' to 'M. Bréchot' ('vous avez là deux numéros qui se valent... je ne sais même pas si...') is a hedged, uncertain personal remark, not a witnessed staged comparison with a level outcome, so no character or status effect is recorded for Bréchot (the reference sheet's Brichot).
